question.prompt:
A bowl is formed by attaching four regular hexagons of side \(1\) to a square of side \(1.\) The edges of the adjacent hexagons coincide, as shown in the figure. What is the area of the octagon obtained by joining the top eight vertices of the four hexagons, situated on the rim of the bowl?

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_10A_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
View the rim from above and fill in its four cut-off corners to make a square. The main task is to identify the corner cuts.

Each hexagon contributes its opposite unit edge to the rim. At two adjacent hexagons, the gap at the bottom fits a unit square, the bowl's base. The symmetry of the two regular hexagons gives an equal square gap at their upper ends. Joining the two rim vertices across this gap therefore makes a diagonal of a unit square, of length \(\sqrt2\).

Consequently the rim has four unit sides alternating with four \(\sqrt2\) sides, arranged as in this top view. Each removed corner is half a unit square.

[Figure 1](figures/2022_AMC_10A_Q21_official_solution_fig1.png)

The enclosing square has side length \(1+1+1=3\). Subtract its four right triangular corners:
\[
3^2-4\left(\frac{1\cdot1}{2}\right)=\boxed{7}.
\]
The answer is B. A complicated rim can have a simpler area when completed to a familiar shape.
solutions.title: Complete the top-view octagon to a square.
